claims.text: Homogeneous noble-metal high-entropy alloy nanoparticles form when precursor reduction is completed before significant atomic diffusion can occur, freezing in a random elemental distribution.
The proposed starting material is a solid precursor containing at least five noble-metal compounds with distinct reduction kinetics.
Rapid heating followed by immediate cooling limits atomic mobility during solid-phase precursor reduction.
Limited free-atom mobility increases the likelihood of forming a random alloy in systems containing many atom types.
Greater atomic mobility permits atoms to rearrange into thermodynamically favored segregated phases.
Faster precursor reduction shortens the time available for atomic diffusion.
When diffusion time is minimized, atoms have insufficient opportunity to migrate and form segregated domains, yielding a uniformly mixed alloy.
Extending the processing window promotes phase separation.
Extending the processing window produces morphologically irregular nanoparticles.
Nanoparticles produced with a shorter reduction window will retain high surface-atom exposure.
Previously reported baseline synthesis conditions can produce heterogeneous phases or elemental segregation.
The mechanism should apply primarily to noble-metal HEA nanoparticles made from solid, mixed or single-source precursors under rapid, non-equilibrium heating and cooling.
The mechanism may not apply to solution-phase syntheses because such systems have inherently high atomic mobility.
Element-specific mixing enthalpies can dominate alloy formation and override the proposed kinetic-window mechanism.
The critical duration below which homogeneous alloying is assured is not quantitatively known.

Changing only the effective reduction duration should produce a systematic transition from homogeneous alloys at shorter durations to segregated or morphologically altered particles at longer durations.
Failure to observe any systematic structural change when the effective reduction window is varied would falsify the claim that this window is the critical governing mechanism.
